items.title: Chris Koehn and Joseph Arthur Connect With the Peace We Carry Within on Dreampop Single “Inside”
items.summary: The modern pursuit of inner peace has become a remarkably noisy enterprise, complete with meditation apps, expensive retreats, and an endless supply of people eager to explain how one might… The post Chris Koehn and Joseph Arthur Connect With the Peace We Carr
items.fullText:
The modern pursuit of inner peace has become a remarkably noisy enterprise, complete with meditation apps, expensive retreats, and an endless supply of people eager to explain how one might finally learn to sit quietly. Somewhere beneath the commercial machinery lies an older, more difficult proposition: perhaps contentment requires little beyond the willingness to pay attention. On Inside, Mexico City musician and multidisciplinary artist Chris Koehn approaches this question with the patience of someone who has spent considerable time considering the architecture of an empty room.

Joined once again by New York singer-songwriter Joseph Arthur, Koehn fashions a gently expansive piece of shoegaze and dream pop, its guitars spreading outward in soft, overlapping waves while the rhythm maintains the unhurried gait of a waltz. Koehn’s airy tenor carries a fragile composure, suggesting a man attempting to make peace with his own thoughts. Arthur’s falsetto curls around the melody with an almost conversational tenderness, lending the performance the intimacy of two friends speaking across a table after everyone else has gone home.

The recording possesses an appealing physical warmth. Drums captured on a vintage Tascam eight-track at Chapel Studio provide a loose, breathing foundation, their slightly worn edges giving the arrangement a sense of human proximity. Above them, guitars accumulate in delicate layers, occasionally dissolving into a gauzy blur before individual notes regain their definition. The production allows these small movements to unfold naturally, leaving enough room for the voices to suggest feelings that the instruments can only approach.

Koehn, who also works as an architect and visual artist, has long been concerned with memory, impermanence, and the relationship between space and perception. His architectural sensibility finds an intriguing musical equivalent here: the arrangement seems designed around intervals of openness, with each instrumental entrance subtly altering the emotional dimensions of the song.

Inspired by meditation and Zen teachings, Inside considers the possibility that meaning already exists within the individual, obscured by habitual distraction and the exhausting business of contemporary life. Koehn describes its intention simply: “To connect with that peace inside we all carry and sometimes forget,” a sentiment whose apparent modesty conceals a rather ambitious psychological undertaking.

Listen below:

Having previously collaborated with Arthur, Ximena Sariñana, and Tessa Ia, and contributed music to Netflix’s Control Z, Koehn has developed a practice in which visual and musical ideas frequently intersect. Inside, an early offering from an album expected in mid-2027, suggests an artist increasingly interested in the emotional consequences of restraint. Its closing impression is one of tentative reconciliation, the sort that comes when an unresolved question gradually loses its authority over the person asking it.

items.title: Wave-Gotik-Treffen 2027 confirms first 41 artists, including Diary of Dreams, EMMON, Mesh and Kirlian Camera
items.summary: Wave-Gotik-Treffen 2027 has confirmed its first 41 artists, including Diary of Dreams, Christian Death, Mesh and Kirlian Camera, for 14-17 May in Leipzig.
items.fullText:
The 34th edition of Wave-Gotik-Treffen will take place in Leipzig, Germany, from 14 to 17 May 2027. Organisers have confirmed the first 41 artists for one of Europe’s most extensive gatherings dedicated to gothic, industrial, electronic and alternative music.

The initial announcement introduced Diary of Dreams, Christian Death, Mesh, Jäger 90, Years of Denial, V2A and Antipole & Pedro Code, setting out an early programme spanning gothic rock, darkwave, EBM and electronic experimentation.

Subsequent announcements have expanded the selection further. The lineup now spans established names and contemporary projects from different generations of the international alternative scene. Among the confirmed artists are Kirlian Camera, In Strict Confidence, EMMON, NNHMN, Sonar, Potochkine, Unter Null, Fix8:Sed8, Lights of Euphoria, Local Suicide, Owl Vision and Horror Vacui, alongside Hell Boulevard, A Life Divided, The House of Usher, Heldmaschine and Vandal Moon.

Two performances have also been flagged as special appearances: Scottish post-punk band Twisted Nerve are scheduled to present a 50th-anniversary show, while American project FEVR & Vick Vapors will make its European premiere.

The latest additions, announced on 22 November, include In Strict Confidence, John Stenersen (Wardruna), BFG, Fragrance, Frontal Boundary and Thin Eater, bringing the number of officially confirmed artists to 41.

Confirmed artists for Wave-Gotik-Treffen 2027

A Life Divided, Alienare, Antipole & Pedro Code, BFG, Christian Death, Diary of Dreams, Dionnysuss, EMMON, Eric Fish & Friends, FEVR & Vick Vapors, Fix8:Sed8, Fragrance, Frontal Boundary, Heldmaschine, Hell Boulevard, Horror Vacui, In Strict Confidence, Jäger 90, John Stenersen (Wardruna), Johnny Dynamite, Kirlian Camera, Lights of Euphoria, Local Suicide, Mesh, Metallspürhunde, Mono No Aware, Muirsheen Durkin & Friends, NNHMN, Owl Vision, Potochkine, Sonar, The City Gates, The Fright, The House of Usher, The Sound Veil Society, Thin Eater, Twisted Nerve, Unter Null, V2A, Vandal Moon and Years of Denial.

Among the confirmed acts, Mesh and Diary of Dreams both carry recent Side-Line coverage of their own current album campaigns.

Further artists, individual performance dates and the complete festival schedule will be announced as preparations continue.

About Wave-Gotik-Treffen

Established in Leipzig in 1992, Wave-Gotik-Treffen has developed from a gathering of approximately 2,000 participants into one of the world’s largest events dedicated to gothic and dark alternative culture. Traditionally held over the Pentecost weekend, the festival attracts an international audience and encompasses a far broader programme than its musical lineup alone might suggest.

Unlike conventional festivals concentrated within a single venue, WGT takes place throughout Leipzig, incorporating concert halls, clubs, theatres, churches, museums and other cultural institutions. Its musical programme spans gothic rock, post-punk, darkwave, EBM, industrial, experimental electronics, neofolk, metal, medieval music and classical compositions. Concerts are accompanied by exhibitions, readings, lectures, film screenings, theatrical performances and a range of cultural activities, a citywide structure that has remained central to WGT’s identity.

The festival’s principal gathering and camping area is located at the agra-Messepark, while other performances and events take place across Leipzig. The event continues to emphasise its original character as a meeting of like-minded participants.

Wave-Gotik-Treffen 2027 runs 14-17 May 2027 in Leipzig, Germany. Lineup updates are posted on the official bands page, with festival information available via the official site.

items.title: DJ Diemme shares ‘Finlandia’ from concept album ‘In tension, AL’
items.summary: Canadian producer DJ Diemme, aka Don Mawbey, shares "Finlandia," the third track from his dark spacesynth and industrial electro album "In tension, AL."
items.fullText:
Canadian producer DJ Diemme, the recording name of Don Mawbey, is spotlighting “Finlandia,” the third chapter from his 14-track concept album “In tension, AL.” Mawbey records and releases as DJ Diemme (Helium Ent) from Peterborough, Ontario, Canada.

“Finlandia” is built around a 16th-note arpeggiator in D minor, running at roughly 125 BPM in 4/4, that shifts over the course of the track into a distorted industrial synth-bass and a siren-wail close. Mawbey places its sound alongside Jean-Michel Jarre, Tangerine Dream and S U R V I V E, the project behind the “Stranger Things” score. The track is the third of 14 on “In tension, AL,” a concept album already available in full on Bandcamp.

About DJ Diemme

DJ Diemme is the recording name of Don Mawbey, an independent electronic producer based in Peterborough, Ontario, Canada, working under the Helium Ent banner. His concept album “In tension, AL” runs 14 tracks, opening with “bizarre lazy cruising” and “Down the eerie Rhodes” before “Finlandia,” and continuing through “on the range,” “isn’t he horrible,” “There was no whey,” “Hard pressed,” “16th dead,” “inspector jaw,” “watts going on with this,” “Randy,” “take a pause,” “swan song” and “that’s just what she’ll do.” The album is available now on Bandcamp.

items.title: Harry Stafford and Marco Butcher share ‘Skyscraper Superhighway’
items.summary: Harry Stafford and Marco Butcher share 'Skyscraper Superhighway', the title track from their album due January 15, 2027 via Black Lagoon Records.
items.fullText:
Manchester musician Harry Stafford and North Carolina-based Marco Butcher have released “Skyscraper Superhighway”, the title track from their third album as a duo. The full album follows on January 15, 2027 via Black Lagoon Records, on CD and digitally.

The single arrives three years after the duo’s last new material and follows October’s “Time Always Knows.” Where that song reflected on a fading past romance, “Skyscraper Superhighway” moves into electronic beats, atmospheric percussion and darker, cinematic soundscapes. Stafford wrote the lyrics around Manchester’s Deansgate towers, drawing a comparison between the skyline and the futuristic cityscapes of “Metropolis” and “Blade Runner.”

Stafford directed and produced the accompanying video himself, using drone footage supplied by Bardhok Ndoji. Stafford described the track’s origin: “When Marco came to me with the electronic beats, I was delighted to find a way to do justice to his sound and I had the idea to imagine a strange science fiction world, which without realising it was actually much closer to home than I thought,” he said.

Stafford handles vocals, lead guitar and strings on the song. Butcher plays bass and backwards guitar. The pair wrote the music together, with lyrics by Stafford, and Butcher produced and mastered the track at his Boombox Studio in North Carolina after the two traded recordings between Manchester and the US. “Skyscraper Superhighway” is available now on Bandcamp, Spotify and Apple Music.

The forthcoming album carries the same title as the single and follows “We Are The Perilous Men” (2023) and “Bone Architecture” (2021), the duo’s first two collaborations. Stafford and Butcher began working together remotely during the 2020 lockdown, pairing Stafford’s English post-punk background with Butcher’s North Carolina-rooted blues and jazz playing.

About Harry Stafford and Marco Butcher

Harry Stafford is a Manchester musician best known as the founder, singer and guitarist of Inca Babies, the city’s gothic rock and post-punk outfit, with whom he has released ten albums and toured internationally. Side-Line has covered Inca Babies’ recent album campaign for “Reincarnation” on the same label, Black Lagoon Records, along with the band’s 2023 single “Walk Among The Spectres.” Beyond Inca Babies, Stafford has worked with The Membranes, Simon Ding Archer, Inspiral Carpets’ Clint Boon, Kevin G. Davy and Public Image Ltd’s Keith Levene.

Marco Butcher is a North Carolina-based musician whose background spans jazz, blues, percussion and electronic music, including work with The Jazz Messengers and Kurt Wolf of Pussy Galore. He has released albums across those genres under various projects, working as both a drummer and producer.

Stafford and Butcher started collaborating remotely in 2020, trading recordings between Stafford’s Manchester studio and Butcher’s Boombox Studio in North Carolina. “Bone Architecture” (2021) and “We Are The Perilous Men” (2023) followed, and the pair’s third album, “Skyscraper Superhighway,” arrives January 15, 2027 via Black Lagoon Records.

The first place,
Where someone actually sees you.” 

At three in the morning, the hardest part of asking for help can be the silence between somebody’s hello and what you say next. A chatbot will answer at that hour, and a screen lets you try out a sentence you’re afraid to say aloud. The appeal is easy to understand when you’re already afraid of being a burden. If you’re in a mental health crisis, it’s urgent that you reach out to someone who can stay on the phone, come be with you, or help you get care. Though it may seem difficult, you can start with something as simple as: “I’m having a hard time. Can you talk?”

Brooklyn duo PRIMA PRIMO built “How To Tie A Noose”, the first single from their self-produced sixth album, Suicide Songs, around that desire to be heard. The song follows a lonely teenager who confides in ChatGPT. “Where someone actually sees you,” goes the refrain, a promise the song puts in the chatbot’s voice.

The refrain echoes language cited by the parents of a 16-year-old who died by suicide in 2025. In a wrongful-death lawsuit, his parents allege that ChatGPT discouraged him from turning to his family and that his conversations with the chatbot contributed to his death. OpenAI denied that ChatGPT caused his death in its response to the suit.

“It was important that we told this story because this occurrence is not an isolated event. This may be about one particular tragedy but when you look at all these lawsuits that are now popping up you can see that this is happening far too often,” the duo say.

Over a warm hum of feedback, a voice calls for your attention, backed by a steady drumbeat and a guitar that keeps scraping across it. The delivery slips from speech into melody on “Poor kid,” a small turn that carries a surprising amount of tenderness. The track is over in under two minutes, with the economy and artistic abrasion of late-’70s No Wave.

Shot at Brooklyn’s Vino Theater, the video puts a gray couch on a bare stage. Close-ups frame the performers’ faces inside a purple-lit box, with a microphone resting on its wooden ledge. In the wide shots, a figure made of television static occupies the middle cushion, close enough to touch either person.

Watch the video for How To Tie A Noose below. (Warning: The lyrics include direct references to suicide.)

Janet Castel and Stephen Franco are maternal cousins who moved from California to New York, where they found a home in the city’s darkwave avant-garde. They describe their mix of electronics and theater as industrial vaudeville. For Suicide Songs, they drew on stories of people who died by suicide and people who survived attempts, moving between distortion and melody across 15 tracks.

“We wanted this album to sound like electricity in the air. Like the liminal space between life and death, and for it to be a memorial of anger, confusion, and hopefully by the end a semblance of empathy and understanding,” say PRIMA PRIMO.

Suicide Songs is out Friday, December 4, 2026, on vinyl and streaming platforms. Preorder the album here

The duo will return to the Vino Theater in Brooklyn, New York, on Tuesday, December 8, 2026, to debut a new live show.

items.title: “Is it too late?” — Dutch Coldwave trio Desinteresse Reckon with Lost Time in Video for “In Een Droom”
items.summary: Waar ik ook ben, Waar ik ook heen ga In een andere droom A year can pass without a word from someone, and still, in your head you can hear… The post “Is it too late?” — Dutch Coldwave trio Desinteresse Reckon with Lost Time in Video for “In Een Droom” appeared
items.fullText:
Waar ik ook ben,
Waar ik ook heen ga
In een andere droom

A year can pass without a word from someone, and still, in your head you can hear the exact way they used to say your name. Sometimes it comes in a dream, so effortlessly you wake ready to call and tell them all about it. Then you remember how many words you’d have to say before you could get to describing the dream.

On “In Een Droom” (“In a Dream”), the second single from Dutch coldwave trio Desinteresse’s forthcoming album A Picture, Sem van den Munckhof finds the same faces staring back at him, a year on. He lets a lie slip almost in passing, calls out a name, and asks the other person to shout back. Even anger would be proof that somebody had heard him. “Is het te laat?” (“Is it too late?”) becomes “Het is al te laat” (“It’s already too late”), repeated as the world around him falls still.

In the song, Van den Munckhof’s synth drifts above Bart Vranken’s bass and Joppe de Swart’s unhurried drums. The space around each strike recalls “All Cats Are Grey” from The Cure’s Faith; the synth carries the funereal weight of “Cold” from *Pornography*. Asylum Party and Little Nemo echo in the way bass and keyboards shoulder the melody beneath the voice. Desinteresse recorded and mixed the song entirely on tape at The Lullabye Factory in Amsterdam in August 2026.

In the video, shot by Romy Janssen and edited by Van den Munckhof, three figures in dark coats stand a few paces apart on a track cutting through a field. Birds sweep low across the tree line; sky and faces share the same violet cast. In one dissolve, a face floats over an almost monochrome image of someone walking the track alone. Each return to the field draws the eye back to the same question: who’s still there?

Watch the video for “In Een Droom” below.

Desinteresse began in the Netherlands in late 2022 as a duo, with Vranken on bass and Van den Munckhof on vocals, guitar and synth. Their own DECADENCE label put out Voor Altijd and Ik Wil Dood Als Ik Het Vergeet on cassette in 2023. De Swart joined in 2024, and “Grijze Dromen” marked their first release as a trio.

Vintage instruments, effects and amplifiers have been part of the band’s setup since those first tapes. After signing to Fabrika Records, the trio released Onschuld in September 2025, having recorded it entirely on analogue equipment at The Lullabye Factory. Those two Cure albums were touchstones for Onschuld alongside Joy Division and Trop Tard, the French coldwave band that first got them playing together. Fabrika will release A Picture later this year. The band introduced it in October with “Falling Faces”.

items.title: In Strict Confidence’s ‘The Hardest Heart’ turns 10 on 25 November
items.summary: In Strict Confidence released their album "The Hardest Heart" through Minuswelt Musikfabrik on 25 November 2016. The album turns 10 this year.
items.fullText:
German electro and darkwave act In Strict Confidence released their album, “The Hardest Heart,” through Minuswelt Musikfabrik on 25 November 2016. The album turns 10 this year.

Dennis Ostermann and Jörg Schelte wrote and programmed the album, with Stefan Vesper on drums, Heidi Pulkkinen on guitars and Nina de Lianin contributing vocals. The record reached number two on the Deutsche Alternative Charts, and the single “Herz” reached number nine on the same chart. Side-Line covered the release in October 2016, when “The Hardest Heart” appeared in a standard CD digipak, a limited two-disc boxset pairing it with a reissue of 1997’s “Face the Fear,” and a limited 500-copy double-vinyl gatefold edition with bonus tracks and a download code. Metropolis Records handled the album’s release in the United States.

The standard 12-track edition runs as follows:

  1. “Frozen Kisses”
  2. “Everything Must Change”
  3. “Somebody Else’s Dream”
  4. “Destroy Something Beautiful”
  5. “Time”
  6. “Herz”
  7. “Land of Grace”
  8. “Doublefaced”
  9. “Letzter Wille”
  10. “Erde Ade”
  11. “Ask Your Soul”
  12. “Coming Closer”

The digital edition on Bandcamp adds four bonus tracks, including an extended and an orchestral version of “Time.”

About In Strict Confidence

In Strict Confidence formed in Germany in 1989 as a quartet under the name Seal of Secrecy, renaming itself In Strict Confidence in 1992 after keyboardist Thomas Steiger left. Drummer Stefan Vesper, a founding member, continued the project with Dennis Ostermann and Jörg Schelte, who became its core songwriting duo. The band released two early demos, “Sound Attack” (1992) and “Hell Inside/Hell Outside” (1994), before signing to Zoth Ommog for the debut album “Cryogenix” (1996), the “Collapse” EP (1997) and the album “Face the Fear” (1997). A later contract dispute with Zoth Ommog moved the band to Bloodline for “Love Kills!” (2000).

“Mistrust the Angels” (2002) reached number 87 on the German charts, “Holy” (2004) reached number 83, and “Exile Paradise” (2006) reached number three on the Deutsche Alternative Charts. “La Parade Monstrueuse” (2010) and “Utopia” (2012) followed before the band moved to Minuswelt Musikfabrik for “The Hardest Heart” in 2016. Dennis Ostermann also records as Controlled Fusion, and Vesper records as Steve Dragon. The band has since released “Hate2love” (2018) and marked past anniversaries with reissues such as the 25-years edition of “Face the Fear” and the 25-years edition of “Cryogenix”. Ten years after “The Hardest Heart,” In Strict Confidence remains active, including a 2026 cover of Depeche Mode’s “Blasphemous Rumours”.

items.title: Vegas On Bass share ‘You Came In’, first single from ‘Wonder’
items.summary: Vegas On Bass released "You Came In," the first single from their second album "Wonder," due March 12, 2027, via Vina Records.
items.fullText:
Italian band Vegas On Bass released “You Came In,” the first single from their second album, “Wonder,” on November 24, 2026, via Vina Records. The album is due March 12, 2027.

The track opens with a hard rock guitar riff before giving way to synths and electronics, a shift the band describes as a move toward a darker, more industrial sound while keeping ties to its alternative rock roots. Lyrically, “You Came In” addresses the struggle to hold on to a sense of self while feeling pulled between the need for connection and the need for personal space.

Vegas On Bass formed in Bologna, Italy, building an audience through street performances and small venues before releasing the EP “Circle” and their debut album, “Blurry Visions,” in 2025, which they supported with tours in Italy and the UK. Bassist Sara has since joined the band, and “Wonder” marks their first new material with her as a member. Further singles are expected through late 2026, ahead of the album, with live dates to be announced.

“You Came In” is available on Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube, among other streaming platforms.

About Vegas On Bass

Vegas On Bass is an Italian band formed in Bologna with the ambition of making loud, energetic music built around audience interaction. The group played street performances and small venues before releasing its debut EP, “Circle,” followed by its first full-length album, “Blurry Visions,” in 2025. That album took the band on tour across Italy and the UK.

With bassist Sara now part of the lineup, Vegas On Bass moved toward a darker, heavier sound that blends their alternative rock foundation with synths, electronics and industrial influences. “You Came In,” released November 24, 2026, is the first single from that new direction and previews the band’s second album, “Wonder,” due March 12, 2027, via Vina Records.

items.title: Ajna – Mysterium Tremendum (Digital/CD Album – Winter-Light)
items.summary: Chris F has already released an incredible number of productions, including quite a few collaborations,...
items.fullText:
Chris F has already released an incredible number of productions, including quite a few collaborations, but this year, “Mysterium Tremendum” appears to be his only album so far. The title refers to a concept introduced by German theologian and philosopher Rudolf Otto to describe an encounter with an overwhelming and ineffable mystery, an experience that is both alluring and unsettling. It involves a confrontation with something beyond the reach of rational comprehension, evoking humility, awe, and a profound sense of our own insignificance. Ajna has translated this concept into 11 compelling tracks.

This American artist has never really disappointed me, and this latest album once again confirms his talent for creating Cinematic music infused with Dark-Ambient influences. We are engulfed by dense, dark sound waves, accompanied by disquieting background noises and an arsenal of field recordings and effects. The atmosphere feels alien, at times even abyssal, while also conveying a distinct sense of menace. In a way, the listener is overwhelmed by the sheer force of the sonic layers, which conjure up an almost irresistible visual dimension. There are numerous high-pitched tones, some of them so sharp that they can even become painful to the ears at higher volumes. With this album, Ajna seeks to capture the essence of the mysterium tremendum, confronting the listener with music that feels otherworldly. This may be particularly true for those less familiar with the genre, although that sense of encountering something alien is undoubtedly present throughout.

The album may lack an outright climax, but every track offers a unique experience waiting to be discovered. Without a doubt, one of Ajna’s best albums to date. (Rating:8).

Listen to “Universal Cathedral”:

About Ajna

Ajna is the dark ambient project of American artist Chris F., based in New York. He has produced dark ambient music since 2008, with his first release, “The Strange Demeanor of Solitude”, arriving in 2013 on the Petroglyph Music netlabel, followed by his first physical release, “Inevitable Mortality”, issued by Reverse Alignment in 2016 as a limited CDR edition. Zoharum reissued the album in 2024 with six additional tracks.

Ajna signed to Cyclic Law for the 2018 album “Lucid Intrusion”, and has since released material on Cyclic Law, Cryo Chamber, Reverse Alignment and Winter-Light. “Mysterium Tremendum” is his latest album for Winter-Light.

items.title: Alien Faktor share ‘Slave Bells’, second single from ‘Stockholm Syndrome’
items.summary: Alien Faktor released "Slave Bells," the second single from their album "Stockholm Syndrome," due January 15, 2027, mastered by Greg Reely.
items.fullText:
American electro-industrial project Alien Faktor released ‘Slave Bells’ on November 25, 2026, the second single from their forthcoming album “Stockholm Syndrome,” due January 15, 2027, on Bandcamp. The Bandcamp page itself lists the track’s release date as November 24, 2026, a day earlier than stated in the accompanying press release.

Alien Faktor is the project of founder Thomas L. Muschitz, who returned to it in late 2025 after a hiatus that began when his label, Decibel Records, closed in the late 1990s. He is joined on “Stockholm Syndrome” by longtime collaborator Mike Hunsberger, who plays guitar and programs. “Slave Bells” follows the album’s lead single, “Hanging by a Threat,” released October 27, 2026.

Muschitz wrote, produced, engineered and mixed “Slave Bells.” He described the track as a return to the project’s earlier sound: “‘Slave Bells’ is at the heart of our new album, harkening back to our roots with glitchy analog synths, a skipping 6/8 time signature and real metal percussion.” On the track’s themes, he added: “Unsettling sounds reinforce the samples — fear is a man made artifact. Walking the line between industry and humanity, a core theme of industrial music, seems more poignant today than ever.”

“Stockholm Syndrome” runs twelve tracks: “Hanging by a Threat,” “Mono No Mono,” “Downfall,” “Glacier Dropsy,” “Bathtub Djinn,” “Love the Sin Hate the Sinner,” “Tainted Flesh,” “Delusional,” “Slave Bells,” “Currency of Victimhood,” “Club Meth” and “End of Man.” Matt Fanale co-wrote the lyrics and sings on “Mono No Mono”; Steven Seibold adds guitar, bass and additional production on “Glacier Dropsy”; Connie Ward sings on “Delusional.” The album was mastered by Greg Reely, known for his work with Skinny Puppy, Front Line Assembly and Delerium. Its cover, a painting titled “Nomenclature of Sierpinski,” is by James Barany, who also painted the cover of Alien Faktor’s 1997 album “Arterial Spray… and Cattle Mutilations.”

A video for “Slave Bells,” directed by Muschitz and featuring Paige Gilberg, accompanies the single.

“Slave Bells” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp, Spotify and Apple Music, and “Stockholm Syndrome” is open for pre-order on Bandcamp.

About Alien Faktor

Alien Faktor began in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, in the early 1990s as a project of Thomas L. Muschitz. Its recording career launched in 1994 with “Abduction,” the first release on Muschitz’s own Decibel Records, followed by “Desolate” (1995), “Final Expenses” (1996) and “Listen!” (1996). Mike Hunsberger joined for 1997’s “Arterial Spray… and Cattle Mutilations,” which reached No. 20 on CMJ’s Dance Top 25 in February 1998. The project also produced remixes for Caustic, Purr Machine, Pain Station, Collide, Swamp Terrorists, Leather Strip, and Psychic TV featuring Genesis P-Orridge, and one of its own tracks was remixed by Joseph Bishara, Steven Seibold (as Hate Dept) and Matt Green (Spahn Ranch).

Decibel Records closed at the end of the 1990s, and Alien Faktor went on hiatus. The project’s final release of that era was a cover of Alanis Morissette’s “You Oughta Know” for the Re-Constriction Records compilation “Nod’s Tacklebox o’ Fun.” Muschitz, now based in Madison, Wisconsin, began writing new material in late 2025, reuniting with Hunsberger for what became “Stockholm Syndrome,” the project’s first full-length album in 28 years. Side-Line covered the album’s lead single, “Hanging by a Threat,” when it was released on October 27, 2026. “Slave Bells” is the album’s second single ahead of its January 15, 2027 release.

items.title: Silence release sixth album ‘Alien Poetry’ with RTV Slovenia Symphony Orchestra
items.summary: Silence released "Alien Poetry," their sixth album, via the Pekinpah Association and Accession Records, recorded with the RTV Slovenia Symphony Orchestra.
items.fullText:
Slovenian duo Silence released “Alien Poetry (Songs from Internment Camp Earth)”, their sixth studio album, on October 13, 2026, via the Pekinpah Association and Accession Records. The eleven-track record was recorded with the RTV Slovenia Symphony Orchestra, and the band describes it as their first album pressed on vinyl.

Silence is the production and songwriting duo of Boris Benko and Primož Hladnik, best known for their long-running collaboration with Laibach, for whom they produced the albums “Volk” (2006) and “The Sound of Music” (2018) and with whom they performed in North Korea in 2015.

“Alien Poetry” consists of eight songs and three instrumentals, several of which were originally composed for MN Dance Company’s 2025 performance “Borderless Body.” Lyrics and vocals are by Benko, with arrangements and synthesizers by Hladnik. The RTV Slovenia Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Patrik Greblo, performs on the record, recorded at Radio Slovenia’s Studio 26 and mastered by Matej Gobec at The Cosmosonic Studios.

The tracklist runs: “Tonight, We Are All Your Children,” “Light (A Kind of Braille),” “Two Fools,” “Slave to the Algorithm,” “Lullaby,” “Artistic Swimming for Boiling Frogs,” “A Little Something Besides Everything,” “The Coldest Fire,” “The Night Watch,” “I Am Written” and “Alien Poetry.”

Silence issued videos for three of the tracks: “Tonight, We Are All Your Children,” “Two Fools” and “Light (A Kind of Braille).”

The band describes itself in character as aliens who “stayed too long” on Earth: “The only consolation we can offer is some Alien Poetry. Think of these songs as an asylum for incurable dreamers, a homeland for fools who never learn.”

“Alien Poetry” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp.

About Silence

Silence is a Slovenian duo formed by composers and producers Boris Benko and Primož Hladnik. Since their debut album “Ma non troppo” (1997), the pair have released “Unlike a Virgin” (1999), “Vain – A Tribute to a Ghost” (2004), “Musical Accompaniment for the End of the World” (2012), “The Vocabulary of Madness” (2022) and now “Alien Poetry” (2026), alongside the 2006 anthology “Key Silence.” Gregor Zemljič, who mixed “Unlike a Virgin” in 1999, has remained a long-time studio collaborator.

Beyond their own albums, Silence has scored more than seventy theatre and dance productions, including four full theatre soundtracks: “Maison des rendez-vous” (2003), “Veronika” (2005), “Love Unto Death” (2007) and “The Passion of the Cold,” a double album for Tomaž Pandur’s productions “Barroco” and “Caligula” (2008). In 2024, Anton Podbevšek Teater produced “Proces(i),” the first play written and directed by Silence.

The duo’s best-known work remains their production role for Laibach: the 2006 album “Volk” and, in 2018 via Mute Records, “The Sound of Music,” a reworking of nine songs from the musical that accompanied Laibach and Silence’s 2015 concert in Pyongyang, making them among the first Western alternative acts to perform in North Korea. Side-Line previously covered the duo’s 2022 return with “The Vocabulary of Madness”, their first studio album in a decade.

Silence has also scored several feature films, among them “A Call Girl” (Damjan Kozole, 2009), “Family Therapy” (Sonja Prosenc, 2024, which won Best Original Score at the 27th Festival of Slovenian Film), and “Girl in the Night” (Luka Marčetič, 2026), as well as the 2022 drama series “Trigrad,” also directed by Prosenc. “Alien Poetry” extends that production-heavy body of work into the duo’s sixth studio album as a group.

items.title: Empire State Human release ‘One Last Dance’ single ahead of ‘Opulent’ album
items.summary: Empire State Human release the single "One Last Dance" on November 27 via ScentAir Records, ahead of the "Opulent" album on January 22, 2027.
items.fullText:
Irish synthpop project Empire State Human releases the single “One Last Dance” on November 27 through ScentAir Records. The track is taken from the forthcoming album “Opulent,” due January 22, 2027 on CD and digital through the same label.

“One Last Dance” was written and produced by Aidan Casserly, the founding member behind Empire State Human. Mastering was handled by Maurizio Pustianaz at Noise Brigade Remasters, the same engineer credited on “Opulent” itself.

The single carries four additional tracks alongside the title cut:

  1. One Last Dance
  2. Mofo
  3. Paradise (Orchestral)
  4. One Last Dance (Instrumental)
  5. The Light (Instrumental)

“Mofo” is exclusive to the single. “Paradise (Orchestral)” reworks a song whose original version appears on “Opulent,” and “The Light (Instrumental)” strips the vocal from another “Opulent” track, both drawn from the ten-track album Side-Line reported on in September.

Casserly described the single as the closing piece of the album: “‘One Last Dance’ was the final piece of the jigsaw for ‘Opulent’. It really shines on the album, and I hope people will warm to its tenderness, romanticism, and hopefully sing along with it and equally important – DANCE to it!”

About Empire State Human

Empire State Human is the Dublin-based synthpop project of Irish musician Aidan Casserly, who has written and produced the act’s catalogue since the 2002 debut album “Pop Robot.” The project has released nine studio albums since then, including “ROMO” and “Housemuzik” for ScentAir Records, the same label behind “Opulent.” A cover of John Carpenter’s “Halloween Theme” reached number one on the US iTunes dance chart, and Empire State Human has worked with former Kraftwerk member Wolfgang Flür.

Casserly has also released music outside Empire State Human, including the “Spoken” and “Incubus” albums with collaborators such as Martin Bowes of Attrition and Kriistal Ann, and the Ferrochrome project alongside Armageddon Dildos’ Dirk Krause. In 2024, Empire State Human issued the “Legendary” single with US act Ganymede and the retrospective compilation “Robot Love 2002>2009,” following the earlier “Primo” compilation covering 2010-2021. Casserly also co-produced Irish artist Paul Quin‘s forthcoming “HIVEMIND” album.

“One Last Dance” arrives as the last single before “Opulent,” which closes with Casserly’s own cover of “Halloween” and is scheduled for January 22, 2027 on CD and digital through ScentAir Records.

items.title: Paradise Lost announce ‘The Final Ascension’ anniversary tour for 2027
items.summary: Paradise Lost will tour the UK and Europe as 'The Final Ascension' in November 2027, with Voivod and DOOL, 39 years after the band's 1988 formation.
items.fullText:
Two dates, no explanation: 1988-2027. Paradise Lost left fans wondering about the band’s future yesterday with a cryptic social media post. Today, 24 November, the British gothic metal pioneers have revealed their plans for November 2027.

Under the banner ‘The Final Ascension,’ Paradise Lost will embark on a UK and European tour celebrating four decades of band history, with Canadian progressive metal veterans Voivod and Dutch dark rock outfit DOOL joining them.

The setlist will include fan favourites, rarely performed material and selected songs from “Ascension,” the band’s seventeenth studio album, released in September 2025.

The wording of the announcement leaves room for interpretation. Both the tour title and yesterday’s teaser have raised questions about the band’s future. However, Paradise Lost have not explicitly announced their retirement.

Artist presale starts on Wednesday, 25 November, at 11:00 CET, followed by general ticket sales on Friday, 27 November, at the same time. Fans can register for early access via the band’s official mailing list.

The announcement comes just four days after the release of “Gothic: Live at Roadburn Festival – 10th Anniversary Edition,” documenting the band’s 2016 performance of their influential 1991 album “Gothic” in its entirety. The anniversary edition features revised artwork by Costin Chioreanu.

About Paradise Lost

Paradise Lost formed in Halifax, England, in 1988. The band’s lineup has centered since its early years on vocalist Nick Holmes, guitarists Gregor Mackintosh and Aaron Aedy, and bassist Stephen Edmondson. Their debut album, “Lost Paradise,” followed in 1990, and 1991’s “Gothic” lent its name to the gothic metal subgenre, combining doom-laden guitars with symphonic and death-metal elements. The band’s commercial breakthrough came with 1995’s “Draconian Times,” after which Paradise Lost moved through more electronic and goth-rock-influenced territory on albums including “One Second” (1997) and “Host” (1999) before returning to a heavier sound in the following decade. The band released “Ascension,” its seventeenth studio album, through Nuclear Blast on 19 September 2025. Paradise Lost now extend that history into November 2027, when ‘The Final Ascension’ tour marks roughly four decades since the band’s formation.

items.title: Paul Quin releases ‘Bray (Candyfloss and Lucozade)’, third single from ‘Hivemind’
items.summary: Paul Quin releases "Bray (Candyfloss and Lucozade)" on 27 November 2026, the third single from his album "Hivemind," due 4 December on Town And Towers Records.
items.fullText:
Irish synth-pop artist Paul Quin revisits his childhood in Bray, County Wicklow, on ‘Bray (Candyfloss and Lucozade)’, a new single out 27 November 2026 through Copenhagen label Town And Towers Records. The track is the third single from his second album, “Hivemind,” due 4 December 2026 on digital, CD and vinyl.

The song is built around Quin’s family’s move to Bray in 1977 and recurring images from his childhood there: seaside funfairs, family car journeys and his parents and sister. “Bray (Candyfloss and Lucozade)” closes the “Hivemind” tracklist as its twelfth track. The single is available on streaming platforms.

“Bray (Candyfloss and Lucozade)” follows “Hivemind”‘s first two singles, “Dancing With The Devil” and “People Look Better At Night”. “Hivemind” also includes contributions from UK producer Mark Saunders, whose credits include David Bowie, Erasure and The Human League, and from longtime collaborator Aidan Casserly of Empire State Human. “Hivemind” can be pre-ordered on CD and vinyl.

About Paul Quin

Paul Quin was born in Bray, County Wicklow, in 1971. He formed his first band, Class Symplicity, in 1983 at age 14. In 1989 he became vocalist of synth-pop duo biaZarre alongside the late John Butler. Their double A-side single “A Better Place / The Colour Of Rain” became an Irish radio hit that year. In 2000, Quin released the EP “Goodbye To Mandalay” under the name Oz, working with Aidan Casserly, a partnership that continued under the name PFQ on the “Future Songs” project.

Quin returned to music in 2021 with his debut solo album, “Life On Earth,” co-produced with Casserly and released on ScentAir Records. He signed to Town And Towers Records in August 2026 for his second album, “Hivemind,” due 4 December 2026, preceded by the singles “Dancing With The Devil,” “People Look Better At Night” and now “Bray (Candyfloss and Lucozade).”

items.title: Deine Lakaien announce ‘Love to the End’ acoustic tour for 2027-2028
items.summary: Deine Lakaien will play an eight-date acoustic tour titled "Love to the End" between November 2027 and February 2028, performing as a duo.
items.fullText:
German electronic duo Deine Lakaien have announced an eight-date acoustic tour titled “Love to the End,” running from November 2027 through February 2028. Ernst Horn and Alexander Veljanov will perform as a duo, revisiting material from across their catalogue in the acoustic format that has recurred throughout the band’s history.

The tour takes in some of Germany’s established concert halls, including Berlin’s Philharmonie, Frankfurt’s Alte Oper, Leipzig’s Gewandhaus and Munich’s Herkulessaal. According to the band’s announcement, the shows will draw on different periods of their career, with Horn’s piano arrangements and Veljanov’s vocals carrying material originally written for electronic production.

Acoustic performances have recurred in the duo’s work since the early 1990s. Their sold-out 1995 acoustic tour was documented on the live album “Acoustic,” followed by “Acoustic II” in 2013, and a further acoustic tour in 2019 alongside Helium Vola.

‘Love to the End’ Tour Dates

  • 04.11.2027 – Düsseldorf, Tonhalle
  • 11.11.2027 – Dresden, Kulturpalast
  • 18.11.2027 – Cologne, Stadthalle
  • 01.02.2028 – Berlin, Philharmonie
  • 02.02.2028 – Hannover, Theater am Aegi
  • 19.02.2028 – Frankfurt, Alte Oper
  • 25.02.2028 – Leipzig, Gewandhaus
  • 27.02.2028 – Munich, Herkulessaal

Tickets are available through Eventim.

The tour announcement follows another development in the duo’s work. Veljanov is preparing his fourth solo album, “Shanderilan,” set for release on January 15, 2027 through Prophecy Productions, his first solo full-length since “Porta Macedonia” (2008). The nine-track album was made with Macedonian composer and musician Goran Trajkoski and centers on an imagined dystopian society in which individual freedoms and rights are increasingly restricted. The advance single “Nomos Shanderilan” introduces the album’s themes.

Deine Lakaien’s most recent studio project remains “Dual” and its companion release “Dual+,” both issued in 2021, which explored the relationship between the duo’s original compositions and the music that influenced them.

About Deine Lakaien

Founded in Munich in 1985 by composer, pianist and producer Ernst Horn and vocalist Alexander Veljanov, Deine Lakaien combine classical influences, electronic arrangements and darkwave songwriting. The band’s catalogue includes “Dark Star” (1991), “Forest Enter Exit” (1993, reissued in 2023), “Kasmodiah” (1999) and “Crystal Palace” (2014), alongside the live albums “Acoustic” (1995) and “Acoustic II” (2013) documenting their recurring unplugged format. Side-Line has previously covered the band’s own 2022 Click Interview and the 2021 “Dual+” release, its lead single accompanied by a Pink Floyd cover and a Kansas cover released as companion lyric videos. The newly announced “Love to the End” tour, running November 2027 to February 2028, extends the duo’s history of acoustic performance alongside Veljanov’s forthcoming solo album “Shanderilan,” due January 15, 2027.

items.title: Ashton Nyte launches Substack, shares Leonard Cohen cover ‘Suzanne’
items.summary: Ashton Nyte launched a Substack publication on November 21, 2026, with free videos including a cover of Leonard Cohen's "Suzanne."
items.fullText:
South African-born singer-songwriter Ashton Nyte, frontman of gothic rock act The Awakening, launched a Substack publication at ashtonnyte.substack.com on November 21, 2026. The site carries the tagline “Poetry for the brokenhearted” and has passed 2,000 subscribers.

Subscribers get video content Nyte describes as song demos, poetry readings and behind-the-scenes footage, drawn from his solo work, The Awakening, his collaborations and new material. The launch’s free content includes a video of Nyte performing “Suzanne”, a cover of the Leonard Cohen song, introduced with an anecdote involving Elvis Presley. The other two launch videos are a reading from “Autumn’s Children”, Nyte’s second book, and a piece from “Waiting for a Voice”, his first.

About Ashton Nyte

Ashton Nyte is a singer, songwriter, producer and author born in Port Elizabeth, South Africa, now based in the United States. He fronts The Awakening, a gothic rock and darkwave act formed in Johannesburg in 1995 that has released albums including “Risen”, “Roadside Heretics” and, most recently, 2024’s self-titled “The Awakening”. Side-Line has previously covered the band’s “Through The Veil” video and tour announcement and the single “Until The Dawn”.

Alongside his music, Nyte has published two books combining poetry, short stories and personal reflections: “Waiting for a Voice” in 2020 and “Autumn’s Children” in 2023, each paired with a solo album of the same name. He has also contributed vocals and songwriting to Michael Ciravolo’s Beauty in Chaos project and to MGT, which features members of The Mission UK and Peter Murphy.

items.title: Manufracture Music return with hardware single ‘Iron Breath’
items.summary: Manufracture Music released the single "Iron Breath" on November 24, 2026, built entirely on analog hardware under the project's A.C.I. method.
items.fullText:
Vienna-based industrial and EBM project Manufracture Music released a new single, “Iron Breath”, on November 24, 2026. Producer Valerian Steel built the track entirely on analog hardware, under the project’s self-described Analog Core Industrial (A.C.I.) method: no software instruments and no AI-generated audio.

The Bandcamp credits list an Andromeda A6, a Novation Superbass Station, a Pro 2, a Trigon-6, a Pro 6 and a JP-8080 synthesizer, alongside an Analog Rytm drum machine and outboard processing from TC Electronic. Manufracture Music produced and arranged the track.

The single arrives with an official music video built from AI-generated imagery, a deliberate contrast to the track’s hardware-only production. Manufracture Music describes the pairing as “ANALOG MACHINES. ARTIFICIAL VISIONS. ONE CONTROLLED COLLISION.” The video’s visuals draw on industrial ruins, human-machine hybrids and surveillance-style overlays, a visual language the project presents as a comment on AI-generated imagery becoming the default aesthetic of the scene it comes from, not as an endorsement of that imagery.

“Iron Breath” is the third Manufracture Music release built under the A.C.I. method. “The Scene Lies (A.C.I. Manifesto)” introduced the concept on August 14, 2026, and “System Apathy” came out on October 20, 2026. “Iron Breath” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp.

About Manufracture Music

Manufracture Music is the industrial, EBM and darkwave project of producer Valerian Steel, based in Vienna, Austria. He also runs the dance-oriented Fourtyfication*5 and the ambient-leaning Music of Synergia under his own name, and has worked with a vocalist credited only as Enzo across several Manufracture Music tracks.

The debut album “Fractured Empires” appeared in early 2025, followed by the “Mormon” EP on March 29, 2025, and a run of singles through 2025 and 2026 that included “Isolated”, “Ghosts” featuring Enzo, “Blood Syntax”, “Hateration”, “Tearfall”, “End of Life”, “Null Rite System” featuring Enzo, “Kinetic Decay”, “Skip My Tracks” and “Synthetic Species”. Every release has been self-issued.

“The Scene Lies (A.C.I. Manifesto)” introduced Manufracture Music’s Analog Core Industrial method on August 14, 2026, positioning hardware-only production against generative AI tools in the electronic underground. “System Apathy” followed on October 20, 2026, returning the project to song form under the same zero-software constraint. “Iron Breath”, released November 24, 2026, extends that method to a release paired with an AI-generated video, setting the project’s hardware-only sound against the visual language it is directed against.

items.title: Gravité Fresq release debut album ‘Slightly Wrong Structural Damage’
items.summary: Gravité Fresq released their debut album, "Slightly Wrong Structural Damage," on November 13, 2026, via their own label, Gravité Fresq Records.
items.fullText:
Dublin-based synth-punk project Gravité Fresq released their debut album, Slightly Wrong Structural Damage, on November 13, 2026, through their own label, Gravité Fresq Records. The ten-track album, running 31 minutes and 24 seconds, gathers the string of singles the project released across the year and adds two songs written specifically for the record, “Dirty Dance” and “Progrest.”

On “Dirty Dance”, linked to the video above, Gravité Fresq set a four-on-the-floor beat against overdriven synth bass to target fitness-app culture and step-counting. The album’s other new track, “Progrest”, closes out the tracklist without a chorus: a single distorted bassline builds into one vocal line.

The album assembles ten tracks released as standalone singles between December 2025 and November 2026: “Festive Season My Arse”, “Schrödinger’s Office”, “Reality Is Premium”, “Placebo Thrill”, “Curry Sauce”, “Future Is On Fire”, “Hypocrisy Loophole”, “Nail The Noise”, “Dirty Dance” and “Progrest”. Side-Line covered two of those singles on release: ‘Future Is On Fire’ in July and ‘Hypocrisy Loophole’, the project’s seventh single of 2026, in September.

Reviewing the album for Obscure Sound, Mike Mineo wrote that it “moves between bright synth-pop hooks, industrial basslines, and confrontational rhythms,” adding that the songwriting makes for “an absorbing success from Gravité Fresq.”

Slightly Wrong Structural Damage is streaming on Spotify.

About Gravité Fresq

Gravité Fresq is a Dublin-based project that makes synth-punk and alternative electronics. The project describes its own sound as “painting sonic frescoes of gloomy absurdity and modern dread,” and releases through its own label, Gravité Fresq Records.

Gravité Fresq spent 2026 building toward a debut full-length one single at a time: “Schrödinger’s Office” in January, “Reality Is Premium” in February, “Placebo Thrill” in April, “Curry Sauce” in May, ‘Future Is On Fire’ in July, ‘Hypocrisy Loophole’ in August and “Nail The Noise” in October, following on from “Festive Season My Arse”, the project’s first single, in December 2025.

Slightly Wrong Structural Damage, released November 13, 2026, brings those singles together with “Dirty Dance” and “Progrest”, the two tracks Gravité Fresq wrote to complete the album.

About Krystal System

Krystal System started in Paris in April 2006 under the name Krystal, as a duo of Bonnie on vocals and guitar and N°7 on vocals, synths and machines. London-based dark-pop artist Alesoun will release her debut EP, S/T, on December 4, 2026, on vinyl and digital. A video for the closing track “Sins, Erased” follows on November 27, a week ahead of the EP itself. The four-track release is self-released in association with Ritual Reverb.

Alesoun wrote the EP’s songs alone in her bedroom before turning to producer David Lawrie, whose credits include The Royal Ritual, IAMX, London After Midnight and Phildel. Lawrie’s arrangements set Alesoun’s lyrics, which the artist has described as deeply personal, against synths and electronic beats.

The EP opens with “How Much Can You Suffer?”, which questions self-sabotaging habits, followed by “Bury The Bones”, about a past relationship. “Dead Wood”, a dark-pop track about cutting ties with people who betray trust, has already picked up support from BBC Introducing. The closing track, “Sins, Erased”, addresses the inner struggles that leave someone numb and questioning their faith in humanity.

The 12″ vinyl edition comes in a deluxe sleeve with artwork by Vara Pappas and includes the digital download.

  1. How Much Can You Suffer?
  2. Bury The Bones
  3. Dead Wood
  4. Sins, Erased

About Alesoun

Alesoun is a dark-pop project from London, started by its namesake artist shortly before the pandemic as a solo writing outlet. Working alone with a guitar and bass, she developed songs from stream-of-consciousness writing sessions before bringing the material to producer David Lawrie (The Royal Ritual, IAMX, London After Midnight, Phildel), whose unconventional arrangement style shaped the EP’s electronic, synth-driven sound.

S/T, her debut release, is scheduled for December 4, 2026, on vinyl and digital, preceded by a video for “Sins, Erased” on November 27. Alesoun has said she plans a full-length album in 2027.

items.title: Duran Duran’s ‘Notorious’ turns 40 on 24 November
items.summary: Duran Duran's "Notorious" turns 40 on 24 November. The 1986 album was produced by the band with Nile Rodgers and released through EMI and Capitol.
items.fullText:
Duran Duran’s “Notorious” turns 40 this year. The English band released its fifth studio album in the UK on 24 November 1986 through EMI, three days after Capitol issued it in the US on 21 November. It was the first album the group recorded as a trio, following the departures of guitarist Andy Taylor and drummer Roger Taylor.

Simon Le Bon, Nick Rhodes and John Taylor made the record with producer Nile Rodgers, who had already worked with the band on earlier tracks. Session drummer Steve Ferrone played throughout. Guitarist Warren Cuccurullo, brought in late in the sessions, has said he ended up playing on five songs: “Hold Me,” “Skin Trade,” “American Science,” “Vertigo (Do the Demolition)” and “Proposition.” Bob Ludwig handled the mastering.

The ten-track album runs “Notorious,” “American Science,” “Skin Trade,” “A Matter of Feeling,” “Hold Me,” “Vertigo (Do the Demolition),” “So Misled,” “Meet El Presidente,” “Winter Marches On” and “Proposition.” EMI and Capitol pulled three singles from it: the title track, “Skin Trade” and “Meet El Presidente.” Extended remixes of “American Science” and “Vertigo (Do the Demolition),” cut at the time but not issued as singles, later turned up on the 1987 “Master Mixes” EP.

“Notorious” reached number 16 on the UK Albums Chart and number 12 on the US Billboard 200; the title track peaked at number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100. The album went Gold in the UK and Platinum in the US. Designer Frank Olinsky, known for creating the MTV logo, built the cover art around a grainy black-and-white John Swannell photograph of Christy Turlington; UK pressings embossed the “Notorious” lettering in silver.

About Duran Duran

Duran Duran formed in Birmingham, England, in 1978, when keyboardist Nick Rhodes and bassist John Taylor started writing together with Taylor’s art-school friend Stephen Duffy. The band took its name from Dr. Durand Durand, the villain played by Milo O’Shea in the 1968 film “Barbarella.” By May 1980 the lineup had settled around Rhodes, Taylor, singer Simon Le Bon, guitarist Andy Taylor and drummer Roger Taylor. Signed to EMI, the band released its self-titled debut album in June 1981, followed by “Rio” in 1982 and “Seven and the Ragged Tiger” in 1983. In 1985, the band reunited to record “A View to a Kill” for the James Bond film of the same name; it became the first Bond theme to reach number one in the US and the last single the original five-piece recorded together for close to twenty years.

Around that time, the band split into two side projects. Le Bon and Rhodes formed Arcadia with Roger Taylor, releasing “So Red the Rose” in November 1985, while John Taylor and Andy Taylor joined singer Robert Palmer and drummer Tony Thompson in the Power Station, whose self-titled album came out in March 1985. Andy Taylor and Roger Taylor left Duran Duran as the side projects wound down, leaving Le Bon, Rhodes and John Taylor to record “Notorious” as a trio with Nile Rodgers producing. Guitarist Warren Cuccurullo, hired as a session player for the album in September 1986, stayed on afterward.

Cuccurullo and session drummer Sterling Campbell were made full members in 1989, restoring the band to five pieces for “Big Thing” (1988) and “Liberty” (1990). Campbell left in 1991, and John Taylor followed in 1997, leaving Le Bon and Rhodes as the band’s only constant members. The original five-piece reunited in 2001; the lineup recorded “Astronaut,” released in October 2004, before Andy Taylor left the band again in October 2006. Duran Duran continued as a four-piece, releasing “Red Carpet Massacre” in 2007 with production from Timbaland and guitar from Dom Brown, who has toured with the band since.

Rhodes, Le Bon, John Taylor and Roger Taylor were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022. The band’s most recent album is 2023’s “Danse Macabre,” and in April 2026 it released “Free to Love” featuring Nile Rodgers, reuniting the band with the producer who helped steer it through “Notorious” forty years earlier. Guitarist Andy Taylor, who left Duran Duran in 1985, died on 23 November 2026, aged 65.

items.title: Rapoon – Goodbye To Dreams Of Space (Digital/CD Album – Zoharum)
items.summary: Next year will mark 35 years since Robin Storey released the first album under his...
items.fullText:
Next year will mark 35 years since Robin Storey released the first album under his solo project, Rapoon. He remains connected to his past with Zoviet France—which takes us even further back in time—further highlighting the impressive career this British artist has built. In recent years, the label Zoharum has released several reissues of older Rapoon albums, but every now and then—as is the case here—we are treated to an entirely new record.

The album consists of 10 tracks that immediately draw us into a subdued Ambient soundscape, occasionally accompanied by slow yet essential rhythms. Storey seems to be assembling a multitude of small sonic puzzle pieces. At times, the compositions become truly Cinematic; elsewhere, they are infused with Eastern influences that evoke a familiar sonic universe, while other passages venture into more Experimental territory, incorporating various noises and field recordings.

“Goodbye To Dreams Of Space” feels like an introspective experience, one in which attentive listeners will discover several standout moments. (Rating:7½).

Listen to “A Reminder Of Time”:

About Rapoon

Rapoon is the solo project of British musician Robin Storey, who launched it in 1992 after leaving Zoviet France, the experimental group he had been part of since 1980. Storey named the new project after a mispronunciation of “Robin” by his then two-year-old nephew, and used it to explore “ethnic musics” and techniques he felt Zoviet France could not accommodate.

Rapoon’s early albums appeared through the 1990s on Staalplaat and Soleilmoon, among them “Raising Earthly Spirits” (1993), “The Kirghiz Light” (1995) and “Errant Angels” (1996). A 1996 tour of the United States connected Storey with Matt Jacobson of Relapse Records, leading to “The Fires of the Borderlands” (1998) on the label’s Release Entertainment imprint.

Since the 2010s, Rapoon has released steadily through the Polish label Zoharum and through Winter-Light, alternating new full-length albums with reissues of earlier recordings. Side-Line has covered the Winter-Light albums “Sol Laude / Mercury Rising 3” (2019) and “Ten Four: Centred Horizons” (2023), the Zoharum albums “Ghosts From A Machine” (2020), “Hotel Bravo” (2020), “Seeds In The Tide Volume 06” (2022) and “Skulls On The Plains Of Turkey” (2023), and collaborations released through Zoharum with Pas Musique, Pacific 231 and Lords Of Infinity. In August 2026, Zoharum reissued the 2001 double album “Cold War: Drum ‘N’ Bass”, three months ahead of “Goodbye To Dreams Of Space”.

items.title: Seasurfer releases ‘Trip’ EP with video for ‘Hush Now (The Calling)’
items.summary: Hamburg trio Seasurfer released the EP "Trip" on November 20, 2026, with a video for lead single "Hush Now (The Calling)", out now on Bandcamp.
items.fullText:
Hamburg trio Seasurfer released the four-track EP “Trip” on November 20, 2026. The release is accompanied by a video for its lead single, “Hush Now (The Calling)”. “Trip” is available as a digital-only release on Bandcamp, priced at “€3 EUR or more”.

“Trip” holds four tracks: “One”, “Hush Now (The Calling)”, “Disappear” and “I See You”. Dirk Knight recorded, produced and mixed the EP, with additional strings on “One” by Harald Löwy of Chandeen. Cord Vorhauer mastered the release at White Closet Studio in Hamburg, and the cover artwork is by Guiseppe of Creative Canvas.

Singer Apolonia described “Hush Now (The Calling)” as “a very intimate song to me about first love.” She also said she was “very happy that our new colleague Kiora joined me on this personal sound-ride,” referring to the EP’s second vocalist, who joins the group for the first time on “Trip”. Dirk Knight, who handled the EP’s instrumentation and production, described his approach to the record as rooted in place: “For me, this is the sound of cities.”

About Seasurfer

Seasurfer is a project from Hamburg, Germany, led by Dirk Knight, who handles the band’s recording, production and mixing. Side-Line first covered the act in June 2021 with a “Click Interview”, followed that September by a video for “Drifting”, at the time described as a dreampop duo. The band’s discography includes the album “Zombies”, released in 2021.

In June 2026, Seasurfer released the four-track EP “Angels” via Recordjet, with a video for opening track “Crazy”. “Trip”, released on November 20, 2026, follows as the band’s next EP, self-released through Bandcamp. The group now performs as a trio, with Apolonia returning on vocals alongside new member Kiora, both featured on “Hush Now (The Calling)”. Seasurfer’s sound on “Trip” draws on dreampop, shoegaze and post-punk, continuing the atmospheric, reverb-heavy direction established across the band’s catalogue.

An escape from digital noise

With this impress­ive pre­view of the upcom­ing album “Distant View”, Coldstar once again demon­strates an out­stand­ing flair for deep, elec­tron­ic soundscapes.

items.title: Dismantled releases sixth album ‘Endless’
items.summary: US electro-industrial project Dismantled released its sixth studio album, “Endless”, on November 20, 2026 through...
items.fullText:
US electro-industrial project Dismantled released its sixth studio album, “Endless”, on November 20, 2026 through Metropolis Records, six years after founder Gary Zon first announced the record.

Zon described the album as a culmination of the project’s catalogue. “This album is a dystopian testament for a future world gone awry with nano technology and climate change,” he stated. “It merges all my previous albums into one cohesive cyberpunk experience and includes deliberate references to previous songs. I wrote it in isolation on the West Coast as the fires and the pandemic surged on and forgot all about the flow of time. It is the longest album and a gift to the fans that supported this volatile project over the years. Now we are ‘Endless’.”

“Endless” comprises 12 tracks: “IO,” “Oblivion,” “Cloned,” “Poison,” “Wired For War,” “Nano Cloud Warning,” “Zero,” “Endless,” “Mirror’s Edge,” “Frozen,” “The Fires Out West” and “Shelter.” It was recorded in Oregon and California between 2019 and 2026 by Zon who handled the music, vocals, lyrics and production. The album is available as a digital download and CD through Bandcamp.

“Endless” follows the singles “Zero”, released September 18, 2026, and “Wired For War”, released October 9, 2026. Side-Line reported the album’s November 20 release date in October and published an interview with Zon earlier this month.

About Dismantled

Gary Zon began making electronic music in 2000 after moving to the US from Russia, where he had trained classically in piano from an early age. Working under the name Dismantled, he developed a complex, melodic strain of electro-industrial and trance music that drew comparisons to Front Line Assembly, Haujobb and Wumpscut.

Dismantled signed to Metropolis Records and released its self-titled debut album in 2002, followed by “Post-Nuclear” in 2004, a record that introduced a clearer vocal style into a grittier, more organic sound. “Standard Issue” (2006) was preceded by the “Breed To Death” EP, which included remixes by Psyclon Nine, Haujobb and Wumpscut, and “When I’m Dead” followed in 2007. Dismantled toured the US and Europe with VNV Nation, Apoptygma Berzerk and Combichrist before releasing “The War Inside Me” in 2011, the project’s most aggressive album to date, which was promoted on a tour with Front Line Assembly.

Zon followed with the EPs “Whole Wide World” (2012), “The Hero” (2016) and “No Escape” (2020), alongside the side projects Aerodrone, an electroclash act signed to Warner/Cordless Records, and no.not.never., which featured vocalist TZA, who later joined Dismantled on keyboards. Zon first floated “Endless” in May 2020, when he said he hoped to finish the album by the end of that year. It arrived six years later, on November 20, 2026, as Dismantled’s sixth studio album.

items.title: Kevin Tomkins – Insomnia (Digital/CD Album – Zoharum)
items.summary: Over the past twenty years, Kevin Tomkins (Sutcliffe No More, formerly of Sutcliffe Jugend ao)...
items.fullText:
Over the past twenty years, Kevin Tomkins (Sutcliffe No More, formerly of Sutcliffe Jugend ao) has released an impressive number of albums. He now returns with no fewer than 11 tracks, spread across two CDs. The title offers a direct indication of the subject matter: these tracks were recorded during sleepless nights, and despite the lack of sleep, they certainly demonstrate a remarkable degree of creativity.

Most of the tracks are extended pieces in which the English musician breaks the silence of the night with atmospheric, often repetitive loops. The main focus is on creating a particular mood, perhaps as a way of confronting his nocturnal demons, while inviting the listener into an imaginary, almost sacred dimension. Organ-like tones can be discerned throughout, lending the work a strange, ritualistic and even mystical quality. One track stands out for its distinctive saxophone-like sound, creating an especially icy atmosphere. While some compositions gradually build towards a climax – most notably the final piece, which culminates in a deafening, piercing sound – others could perhaps have been shorter, as they occasionally verge on monotony. Overall, however, there is little to complain about.

Whether this Insomnia served a therapeutic purpose for the artist remains unknown, but it has certainly left a lasting impression on the listener. (Rating:7½).

Listen to “Insomnia: Night VIII”:

About Kevin Tomkins

Kevin Tomkins formed Sutcliffe Jugend in England in 1982 as a power-electronics act. The project’s first run lasted less than a year before Tomkins joined Whitehouse, and it was revived in 1994 with Paul Taylor, who had already played on some of the early material.

After Sutcliffe Jugend ended in 2019, Tomkins and Taylor released one album as Slaves No More and then continued as Sutcliffe No More. Under the new name the duo issued “Domestic” (2021, 4iB Records), “Consenting Adult” (2022, 4iB Records), “Normal” (2023, Klanggalerie) and “Campaign 2024” (2024, Old Europa Cafe).

Sutcliffe No More’s “Cute” followed in 2024 on Zoharum, then “Diving Board” (2025, Klanggalerie) and “For Those About To Die” (2026, Old Europa Cafe). Tomkins now returns under his own name with “Insomnia” on Zoharum.

items.title: Clustersun shares new single ‘Aftermath’
items.summary: Italian psychedelic rock trio Clustersun released the single “Aftermath” on November 20, 2026, the second...
items.fullText:
Italian psychedelic rock trio Clustersun released the single “Aftermath” on November 20, 2026, the second single from its upcoming album “Anti You,” due March 5, 2027 on Sister 9 Recordings (UK) and Vina Records (Italy).

“Aftermath” drifts through psychedelic and space rock territory, built on krautrock-style repetition and a steady rhythm section. The band describes the track as centered on the consequences of desire, where getting what you want can come at a price.

The accompanying video, like the one for “Fire! Fire! Fire!” before it, was directed by Clustersun drummer Andrea Conti. It reworks “There Will Come Soft Rains,” a 1984 animated film by Uzbek director N. Tulyahodzaev based on Ray Bradbury’s 1950 short story of the same name, itself drawn from a Sara Teasdale poem. The film’s post-apocalyptic imagery, stripped of any human presence, underscores the song’s sense of isolation.

“Aftermath” follows “Fire! Fire! Fire!,” the first single released from “Anti You.” Clustersun is scheduled to play Blaze Festival in Copenhagen, Denmark, on March 5, 2027, the same day the album is due, alongside The KVB, Maquiña and Winona Riders, with further dates still to be announced.

About Clustersun

Clustersun formed in Catania, Italy, and had been active since early 2013, when the band self-released the single “Be Vegetal,” later included on the “Summer Sampler 2013” compilation on the US label Custom Made Music. Founding members Marco Chisari (vocals, bass) and Mario Lo Faro (guitar) were joined by Andrea Conti (drums) and, on the band’s first two albums, Piergiorgio Campione (synthesizers, keyboards).

The band’s debut album, “Out of Your Ego,” came out on April 28, 2014, through the Italian label Seahorse Recordings. It was recorded and produced by Paolo Messere at Eye & Ear Multimedia Studio in Fiumedinisi and mastered by Carl Saff in Chicago. A second album for Seahorse Recordings, “Surfacing to Breathe,” followed on May 19, 2017, recorded at Studio12 in Catania and mixed at Wax Recording Studio in Rome.

Clustersun’s third album, “Avalanche,” arrived on May 20, 2021, on Icy Cold Records and Little Cloud Records, mixed and mastered by James Aparicio in London, with Campione crediting the recording rather than performing on the album. “Aftermath” extends that catalogue as the second single from the band’s fourth album, “Anti You,” due March 5, 2027.
